page: Google Cloud Platform f1-micro is a burstable, budget-oriented virtual machine instance belonging to the f1 family. It features 1 vCPU allocated from a shared physical Intel Xeon core on the x86_64 architecture, paired with 0.6 GB of system memory. The instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The underlying Intel Xeon processor supports hardware flags such as AVX, AVX512F, AES cryptography, and hyper-threading.

Benchmark data places the f1-micro in the bottom 10% of tested servers across all key metrics. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU performance scores both register at 384.79. Memory bandwidth is highly constrained, with a read-only small block cached speed of 80.8 GB/sec and a large block write speed of 0.2 GB/sec. In application-level tests, the instance achieves 0.24 million operations per second for Redis SET operations and a static web serving throughput of 0.22 GB/sec.

Due to its shared-core architecture and minimal memory footprint, the f1-micro represents a low-cost entry point for basic cloud hosting. The primary tradeoff is its severely limited processing power and memory capacity, which makes it unsuitable for resource-intensive applications. It is designed for lightweight workloads such as simple cron jobs, basic development environments, low-traffic static web serving, or small utility scripts that do not require sustained CPU performance.
